verdict: 2026-07-27 19:33:34 PDT — The overall shape is sound and proportionate: one Bash CLI is idiomatic for this repository, jq is already an estate dependency, subprocess boundaries give both skills one implementation, and behavioral fixtures address the actual failure generator. Reusing the compiler in check-plan is not circular provided the checker independently reconstructs the compiler inputs from the bound target; golden behavioral fixtures are the independent oracle for compiler correctness. I would trim the first delivery to the plan-side consumer and close two contract seams before implementation.

findings.title: Make check-plan re-derive from authoritative inputs
findings.locus: Design sketch — Compilation, not just validation; Open question 3
findings.claim: The sketch alternately describes compile-plan as consuming a unit-map and signals, and leaves open whether the library derives them itself. Because check-plan accepts only plan.json, an implementation could reuse the candidate plan's unitMap/signals when recompiling. That would make completeness circular: coherently tampered inputs and rows could validate each other, and a source edit that does not alter row arithmetic could pass.
findings.alternative: Define one internal compiler taking a target root, the recorded detection profile, and normalized patches. It must derive the fingerprint, unit-map, and deterministic signals from the target itself. check-plan should verify source.contentFingerprint, invoke that compiler from those authoritative inputs, and compare the compiler-owned structural projection; narrative fields remain outside the comparison. Golden fixtures for every Table-P rule independently test the compiler.
findings.win: Centralizes unit-map and signal derivation, eliminates the candidate-derived-input seam, and makes one check reject source drift, omitted rows, suppressed upgrades, and misapplied patches without duplicating Table P.

findings.title: Ship the plan-side slice first
findings.claim: As drafted, build-manifest, check-report, adjudicate, and the capability table would establish public behavior solely from speculative fixtures before /deep-audit-run exists. Their exact envelopes, ledger states, and evidence shapes are integration contracts most likely to change when the live engine is built; landing them now makes the foundational story larger without proving an actual seam.
findings.alternative: Take Option B: ship fingerprint, resolve-units, compile-plan, check-plan, the /deep-audit refactor, and their behavioral tests now. Add the execute-side subcommands and capability table to the same library in the engine story, alongside their first live consumer.
findings.win: Removes three unconsumed subcommands and their speculative fixture matrix from this story, while preserving the one-library architecture and allowing each execute-side contract to be tested against its real caller when introduced.

findings.title: Name the executable JSON-schema gate
findings.locus: Design sketch — JSON is the interface; .claude/skills/deep-audit/plan-schema.json
findings.claim: jq is appropriate for transformation and semantic assertions, but it is not a Draft-7 validator. The sketch says schemas own shape and exit status is the verdict without naming how check-plan validates that shape. Merely parse-checking JSON leaves malformed contracts admissible; manually restating required fields, types, enums, and additionalProperties in jq creates the same duplicated-rule seam this story exists to remove.
findings.alternative: Keep jq for compilation, but make check-plan invoke one declared, preflighted JSON-Schema validator against plan-schema.json before semantic recompilation, and pin that validator in CI/deployment requirements. If adding that dependency is rejected, explicitly make a single jq contract canonical and generate the external schema from it rather than maintaining two handwritten shape definitions.
findings.win: Eliminates a second handwritten shape contract and ensures a zero exit means both schema-valid and semantically complete, closing an otherwise untested malformed-input path.
